fields.sample_size: policy-and-practice case study of Kitui County, Kenya (about 400,000 people rely on surface water; the water-fund mechanism grew from under USD 50,000 to over USD 190,000 a year as users rose from 15,000 to over 75,000; FundiFix serves about 55,000 people; 755 people (528 men, 227 women) attended sub-county workshops)
fields.effect_estimate: Describes devolved water governance in Kitui County: county water policy and legal instruments, a county water fund (WSMTF), the FundiFix professionalised maintenance service model and sub-county participation workshops, and the politics of devolution (county-level capture, funding unpredictability). Reports growth in fund resources and users covered but no controlled evaluation. Practice-based review by authors involved in the programmes; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: policy and practice review of a county devolved-governance case (documents, programme data, workshops)
fields.section: Full text: Introduction (Kitui water context); policy and legal framework; county water fund and FundiFix; sub-county workshops; Discussion
fields.exact_location: Introduction (Kitui water context); policy and legal framework; county water fund and FundiFix; sub-county workshops; Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a policy-and-practice review of water governance in Kitui County, Kenya, read in full text 2026-10-04. A county water fund and a professional maintenance service (FundiFix, about 55,000 people) expanded coverage of reliable service; devolved governance brings opportunities and political risks. Descriptive, programme-involved authors.
pdf_note: Frontiers in Water 4:1022730 (2022), about 76,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction (vague) replaced with programme figures. Authors include programme implementers (potential conflict of interest in the description of FundiFix).
